correctness.rationale: Checked exact denominator reindexing n→m=n-1 against arXiv:2603.28806v1 Theorem 2.2. S_alpha(r) is strictly increasing in radius and strictly decreasing in alpha, and diverges at r↑1 for each finite alpha; implicit differentiation yields rho'>0. T_alpha'=S_alpha, so R_alpha'=-partial_alpha T_alpha(rho)>0 without missing endpoint derivative. Put beta=1/alpha, split Σ rho^m/(m+beta)=-log(1-rho)-psi(1+beta)-gamma+o(1) using uniform absolute β/m² bound; obtain log(1/(1-rho))=a alpha/2+psi(1+1/alpha)+gamma+o(1). Absolute expansion T_alpha(1)=2/alpha-2(pi²/6-1)/alpha²+O(alpha^-3) and exponentially small endpoint truncation complete the R asymptotic. At alpha=0, rho=a/(a+2), R=a+2log(1-rho). Independent numerical quadrature at M=1, alpha=0,1,3,10 matches increasing radii and contrasting scales. This concerns guaranteed coefficient-series radii only; no extremality among all harmonic maps.
